describes: One run per fixture: which slice to execute, and which scenarios that fixture is expected to turn red. The expected sets are a prediction. Where a run disagrees, the observation wins and the difference is written up as a finding - bending a fixture until it matches the table would defeat the entire exercise.

runs.specSaysRed: nothing; the baseline is the control
runs.note: Every scenario in the suite. @never matches no tag, so the expression selects all of them.

runs.tags: @TC-77 or @TC-177 or @TC-76 or @TC-176 or @TC-01 or @TC-02 or @TC-05
runs.note: TC-177 is the destination mirror of TC-77, added by work package B after section 4's table was written. A confidence floor is a property of the matcher, not of a field, so a lowered floor necessarily moves both. Expecting only TC-77 would be expecting the suite to be blind on one field.

runs.tags: @TC-76 or @TC-176 or @TC-77 or @TC-01 or @TC-02 or @TC-03 or @TC-04 or @TC-05
runs.note: TC-176 is the destination mirror, for the same reason as mut-floor-lowered. TC-01 to TC-05 are the controls: exact matches never consult the floor.

runs.tags: @TC-78 or @TC-178 or @TC-79 or @TC-01 or @TC-02 or @TC-03 or @TC-06
runs.note: TC-178 is the destination mirror. TC-79 is the reject side of the same cap and must stay green: narrowing a cap cannot start accepting something it already rejected.

runs.tags: @TC-05 or @TC-105 or @TC-80 or @TC-180 or @TC-01 or @TC-04 or @TC-06 or @TC-07
runs.note: TC-105 and TC-180 are the destination mirrors. The corrected city is still right in all four, so only the confidence assertion added by B-5 can see the mutation; TC-04 (padding only, no internal run) is the control that keeps trimming and collapsing apart.

runs.tags: @TC-22 or @TC-23 or @TC-29 or @TC-46 or @TC-47 or @TC-113 or @TC-115 or @TC-117 or @TC-177 or @TC-13 or @TC-15 or @TC-17 or @TC-77
runs.note: The spec asked only for one destination case. The slice covers all three destination outcome classes (unmatched, missing, ambiguous) plus the two multi-reason scenarios, against origin controls that must not move. TC-23 and TC-47 are red because their second reason changes, not their first.
The three genuine ambiguity scenarios are the controls: the mutation must break precedence without breaking ambiguity reporting, or the result says nothing about precedence.

runs.tags: @TC-06 or @TC-07 or @TC-08 or @TC-09 or @TC-10 or @TC-11 or @TC-12 or @TC-76 or @TC-78 or @TC-01 or @TC-02 or @TC-03 or @TC-04 or @TC-05 or @TC-80
runs.note: TC-76 and TC-78 are boundary rows added by B-2 that also assert the fuzzy path, so they move with the rest. Every corrected city is still right, which is the point: nothing but the confidence assertion catches this.
The other malformed scenarios are the controls: they assert the reason and nothing else, so they stay green and show that only the assertion B-6 added can see the invented id.

runs.tags: @TC-22 or @TC-23 or @TC-50 or @TC-46 or @TC-41 or @TC-30 or @TC-70
runs.note: TC-46 also asserts the original since B-4 and B-6, so it moves too. TC-41 is the control that matters: the normalised payload still validates against the flagged schema, so the schema layer cannot catch this and the field-level comparison has to.
TC-53 publishes two messages on one key as well, but they are identical, so reversing them is unobservable; it is the control proving the assertion is about order rather than about count.
TC-63 is the one B-7 was written for: before the poll result was asserted, it compared two empty key sets and passed against a service that had produced nothing at all.

TC-30 and TC-21 are declared controls, and they are expected to fail anyway. B-7 rewrote the key assertion in MessageContractSteps to locate its message by payload, but the routing step that runs before it (RoutingSteps, via MessageCollector.receivedFor) still correlates by key. A service that emitted the wrong key therefore fails every scenario that awaits a message, and reports it as nothing arrived rather than as a wrong key. That is a finding about the harness, not about these two scenarios, and it is the same spread the 2026-09-06 run against the real service saw on TC-30 and TC-31.

runs.tags: @TC-32 or @TC-34 or @TC-30 or @TC-31 or @TC-33 or @TC-41 or @TC-42
runs.note: Every positive assertion about the flagged route still passes, which is why TC-31 and TC-41 are the controls. TC-42 is the control that matters most: TEST_SUITE_SPEC section 7.5 claims it is a second, independent mechanism catching a flagged booking on the enriched topic, and DEF-111 says it is not, because it validates a flagged payload in isolation and never sees where that payload was published. This run re-tests that claim empirically. TC-42 staying green while the leak actually happens is the defect, not a passing control.
TC-61 is the count-only check and is the whole argument for the fixture: every total still matches, so it stays green while TC-60, which compares identities since B-8, does not.
